What is PHP: PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is a widely-used open-source scripting language designed for web development. PHP code is executed on the server, generating HTML that is sent to the client. It can be embedded directly into HTML and works seamlessly with databases.
PHP Syntax: PHP code is enclosed in <?php ... ?> tags. Statements end with semicolons. PHP can be embedded anywhere in HTML. Variables start with $. Whitespace is ignored. The closing ?> is optional at the end of a file (recommended to omit to prevent accidental output).

<?php
// This is a comment
echo "Hello World";

$name = "Alice";
$age = 30;
echo "$name is $age";

// No closing tag at end of pure PHP files
Variables: PHP variables start with $ followed by a letter or underscore. They are dynamically typed and case-sensitive. Variables can be assigned by value or by reference (&). Variable variables ($$var) allow dynamic variable names.

<?php
$name = "Alice";
$age = 30;
$price = 19.99;
$is_active = true;

// By reference
$original = 10;
$ref = &$original;
$ref = 20;  // changes $original too

// Variable variables
$varName = "foo";
$$varName = "bar";  // $foo = "bar"
echo $foo;  // bar
Data Types: PHP supports: string, int, float, bool, array, object, null, resource. Use var_dump() to inspect type and value. gettype() returns the type name. Type juggling happens automatically; use strict comparison (===, !==) to avoid surprises.

<?php
$s = "Hello";          // string
$i = 42;                // int
$f = 3.14;              // float
$b = true;              // bool
$a = [1, 2, 3];         // array
$n = null;              // null

var_dump($s, $i, $f, $b, $a, $n);

// Type juggling
var_dump('5' == 5);     // true (loose)
var_dump('5' === 5);    // false (strict)
Constants & Magic Constants: define() defines runtime constants. const keyword defines compile-time constants (must be in top-level scope). Magic constants like __FILE__, __DIR__, __LINE__, __CLASS__, __METHOD__ change based on where they're used.

<?php
define('SITE_NAME', 'MyApp');
const VERSION = '1.0.0';

echo SITE_NAME;
echo VERSION;

// Magic constants
echo __FILE__;     // current file path
echo __DIR__;      // directory of current file
echo __LINE__;     // current line number
echo __CLASS__;    // current class name
PHP Tags & Output: Multiple ways to output: echo (language construct), print (returns 1), printf (formatted), var_dump (debug info). Short echo tag <?= is shorthand for <?php echo. Always available in PHP 5.4+.

if/else/elseif: Standard conditional execution. elseif (one word) is the recommended form over else if (two words, requires braces). Use switch for many conditions on the same variable. Match (PHP 8+) is a stricter switch without loose comparison.

<?php
$score = 85;

if ($score >= 90) {
    echo 'A';
} elseif ($score >= 80) {
    echo 'B';
} else {
    echo 'C';
}

// Alternative syntax with :
if ($score >= 80):
    echo "Pass";
endif;
switch & match: switch compares loosely (==). Use break to prevent fall-through; default for no match. match (PHP 8+) compares strictly (===), returns a value, and doesn't require break. match throws UnhandledMatchError on no match.

<?php
$status = 404;

switch ($status) {
    case 200:
        echo 'OK';
        break;
    case 404:
        echo 'Not Found';
        break;
    default:
        echo 'Unknown';
}

// match (PHP 8+)
$result = match ($status) {
    200 => 'OK',
    404 => 'Not Found',
    500 => 'Server Error',
    default => 'Unknown',
};
echo $result;
for & foreach: for loops use counter (init; condition; increment). foreach is the preferred way to iterate arrays: foreach($arr as $value) or foreach($arr as $key => $value). Use break to exit, continue to skip iteration.

<?php
// for loop
for ($i = 0; $i < 5; $i++) {
    echo "Count: $i\n";
}

// foreach with array
$fruits = ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'];
foreach ($fruits as $fruit) {
    echo $fruit;
}

// foreach with key => value
$ages = ['Alice' => 30, 'Bob' => 25];
foreach ($ages as $name => $age) {
    echo "$name is $age";
}
while & do-while: while runs before checking condition (may run 0 times). do-while runs at least once. Use with caution to avoid infinite loops. Common for reading data until exhausted.

<?php
$i = 0;
while ($i < 3) {
    echo "While: $i\n";
    $i++;
}

// do-while runs at least once
$j = 0;
do {
    echo "Do: $j\n";
    $j++;
} while ($j < 3);

// Reading file line by line
$handle = fopen("file.txt", "r");
while (($line = fgets($handle)) !== false) {
    echo $line;
}
fclose($handle);
Alternative Syntax: PHP provides alternative syntax for control structures using colons and endif/endwhile/endfor/endforeach/endswitch. This is commonly used in templates to mix PHP with HTML cleanly.

Welcome back!

Please log in

Defining Functions: Functions are defined with the function keyword. They can have typed parameters and return types (PHP 7+). Default parameter values are supported. Use return to return a value; functions without return return null.

<?php
function greet(string $name): string {
    return "Hello, $name!";
}

echo greet('Alice');

// Default parameters
function multiply(int $a, int $b = 2): int {
    return $a * $b;
}

echo multiply(5);     // 10
echo multiply(5, 3);  // 15
Variable Scope: Variables defined outside functions are global — use global keyword to access them inside functions. Static variables persist between calls. Function parameters are local. The $GLOBALS superglobal provides access to all global variables.

<?php
$globalVar = 'outside';

function test() {
    global $globalVar;
    echo $globalVar;
    
    static $count = 0;
    $count++;
    echo $count;
}

test();  // outside, 1
test();  // outside, 2

// Via $GLOBALS
function test2() {
    echo $GLOBALS['globalVar'];
}
Type Declarations: PHP 7+ supports scalar type declarations: int, float, string, bool, void, iterable, mixed (PHP 8+), never (PHP 8.1+). Nullable types use ? prefix (e.g., ?string). Union types (PHP 8+) use | (e.g., int|string). Strict mode enabled with declare(strict_types=1).

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

function add(int $a, int $b): int {
    return $a + $b;
}

// Nullable type
function find(?string $id): ?array {
    if ($id === null) return null;
    return ['id' => $id];
}

// Union type (PHP 8+)
function format(int|string $value): string {
    return (string) $value;
}
Anonymous Functions & Closures: Anonymous functions (closures) can be assigned to variables or passed as arguments. Use function ($arg) use ($var) { ... } to import variables from the outer scope. Arrow functions (PHP 7.4+) provide shorter syntax with fn($arg) => expr.

<?php
// Anonymous function
$greet = function(string $name): string {
    return "Hello, $name!";
};
echo $greet('Alice');

// Closure with use
$prefix = "User: ";
$formatName = function(string $name) use ($prefix): string {
    return $prefix . $name;
};

// Arrow function (PHP 7.4+)
$multiply = fn($a, $b) => $a * $b;
echo $multiply(3, 4);  // 12

// As callback
$numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4];
$squared = array_map(fn($n) => $n * $n, $numbers);
Variable Functions & Callbacks: If a variable name has parentheses appended, PHP looks for a function with that name. call_user_func() and call_user_func_array() call callbacks. Useful for dynamic dispatch and event handling.

<?php
function hello() { echo "Hello!"; }
function bye() { echo "Bye!"; }

$func = 'hello';
$func();  // calls hello()

$func = 'bye';
$func();  // calls bye()

// With parameters
function add(int $a, int $b): int { return $a + $b; }
call_user_func('add', 3, 4);
call_user_func_array('add', [3, 4]);

Indexed Arrays: PHP arrays are ordered maps. Indexed arrays use numeric keys starting from 0. Create with array() or short syntax []. Access with $arr[index]. Count elements with count(). Manipulate with array_push, array_pop, array_shift, array_unshift.

<?php
$fruits = ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'];
echo $fruits[0];  // apple

$fruits[] = 'date';           // append
array_push($fruits, 'elderberry');
$last = array_pop($fruits);
$first = array_shift($fruits);
array_unshift($fruits, 'apricot');

echo count($fruits);
print_r($fruits);
Associative Arrays: Associative arrays use string keys. Useful for key-value mappings and structured data. Access with $arr['key'] or $arr[$key]. Check key existence with isset() or array_key_exists(). Merge arrays with array_merge().

<?php
$user = [
    'name' => 'Alice',
    'age' => 30,
    'email' => 'alice@example.com'
];

echo $user['name'];

// Check key
if (isset($user['email'])) {
    echo "Email exists";
}

// Merge
$defaults = ['role' => 'user', 'active' => true];
$user = array_merge($defaults, $user);

// Iterate
foreach ($user as $key => $value) {
    echo "$key: $value\n";
}
Multidimensional Arrays: Arrays can contain other arrays for nested data structures. Access with multiple indices ($arr[0]['name']). Useful for representing complex data like tables, matrices, or nested records.
Array Functions: PHP has a rich set of array functions: array_map (transform), array_filter (filter), array_reduce (aggregate), array_merge (combine), array_diff (difference), array_intersect (common), array_keys (get keys), array_values (get values), sort functions (sort, rsort, asort, ksort, usort).

<?php
$numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Transform
$squared = array_map(fn($n) => $n * $n, $numbers);

// Filter
$even = array_filter($numbers, fn($n) => $n % 2 === 0);

// Reduce
$sum = array_reduce($numbers, fn($carry, $n) => $carry + $n, 0);

// Sort
$fruits = ['cherry', 'apple', 'banana'];
sort($fruits);              // ascending
rsort($fruits);             // descending
asort($fruits);             // maintain keys
ksort($fruits);             // sort by keys
SPL Data Structures: SPL (Standard PHP Library) provides built-in data structures: SplStack, SplQueue, SplHeap, SplPriorityQueue, SplFixedArray, SplObjectStorage. These are more memory-efficient than plain arrays for specific use cases.

<?php
// Stack (LIFO)
$stack = new SplStack();
$stack->push('first');
$stack->push('second');
echo $stack->pop();  // second

// Queue (FIFO)
$queue = new SplQueue();
$queue->enqueue('first');
$queue->enqueue('second');
echo $queue->dequeue();  // first

// Fixed array (better memory)
$fixed = new SplFixedArray(3);
$fixed[0] = 'a';
$fixed[1] = 'b';

Classes & Objects: Classes define blueprints for objects. new creates instances. $this refers to the current instance. Properties and methods can be public, protected, or private. Constructor __construct() initializes properties. Type declarations work on properties (PHP 7.4+) and promoted properties (PHP 8+).

<?php
class User {
    public function __construct(
        private string $name,
        private int $age
    ) {}
    
    public function greet(): string {
        return "Hello, I'm {$this->name}";
    }
    
    public function getName(): string {
        return $this->name;
    }
}

$user = new User('Alice', 30);
echo $user->greet();
echo $user->getName();
Inheritance: extends creates a child class that inherits parent methods and properties. Use parent:: to call parent methods. Override methods by redefining them. final keyword prevents overriding. abstract classes define base functionality with abstract methods.

<?php
class Animal {
    public function __construct(protected string $name) {}
    
    public function speak(): string {
        return "$this->name makes a sound";
    }
}

class Dog extends Animal {
    public function speak(): string {
        return "$this->name barks";
    }
}

$dog = new Dog('Buddy');
echo $dog->speak();

// Abstract class
abstract class Shape {
    abstract public function area(): float;
}

class Circle extends Shape {
    public function __construct(private float $radius) {}
    public function area(): float {
        return pi() * $this->radius ** 2;
    }
}
Interfaces & Traits: Interfaces define contracts with method signatures. A class can implement multiple interfaces. Traits enable horizontal code reuse — they're like partial classes. Use traits with the use keyword inside a class.

<?php
interface Logger {
    public function log(string $message): void;
}

interface Notifier {
    public function send(string $to, string $message): void;
}

trait Timestampable {
    public function getTimestamp(): string {
        return date('Y-m-d H:i:s');
    }
}

class AppLogger implements Logger, Notifier {
    use Timestampable;
    
    public function log(string $message): void {
        echo "[{$this->getTimestamp()}] $message";
    }
    
    public function send(string $to, string $message): void {
        mail($to, "Alert", $message);
    }
}
Namespaces: Namespaces organize code and prevent naming conflicts. Declare with namespace at file top. Import with use keyword. Aliases with use ... as .... Fully qualified names start with \ (global namespace). Follow PSR-4 for autoloading.

<?php
namespace App\Models;

class User {
    // ...
}

// Another file
namespace App\Controllers;

use App\Models\User;
use App\Helpers\Format as Fmt;

$user = new User();
Fmt::formatText('hello');
Static Methods & Properties: Static members belong to the class, not instances. Accessed with :: (Scope Resolution Operator). self:: refers to the current class, static:: refers to the called class (late static binding). parent:: accesses parent class.

<?php
class Database {
    private static ?Database $instance = null;
    
    public static function getInstance(): self {
        if (self::$instance === null) {
            self::$instance = new self();
        }
        return self::$instance;
    }
    
    private function __construct() {}
    
    public static function connect(): string {
        return "Connected";
    }
}

$db = Database::getInstance();
echo Database::connect();

Reading Files: file_get_contents() reads entire file as string. file() reads into array by lines. fopen() with fread()/fgets() provides streaming access. feof() checks end-of-file. Always close with fclose(). Use file_exists() and is_readable() to check first.

<?php
// Simple read
$content = file_get_contents('file.txt');

// Read into array
$lines = file('file.txt');

// Streaming read
$handle = fopen('file.txt', 'r');
if ($handle) {
    while (($line = fgets($handle)) !== false) {
        echo $line;
    }
    fclose($handle);
}

// Check before reading
if (file_exists('file.txt') && is_readable('file.txt')) {
    $content = file_get_contents('file.txt');
}
Writing Files: file_put_contents() writes string to file (replaces). Use FILE_APPEND flag to append. fopen() with w (write), a (append), x (create exclusive) modes. flock() for file locking. fwrite() for streaming writes.

<?php
// Simple write
file_put_contents('file.txt', 'Hello World');

// Append
file_put_contents('file.txt', "\nNew line", FILE_APPEND);

// With stream
$handle = fopen('file.txt', 'w');
flock($handle, LOCK_EX);
fwrite($handle, "Line 1\n");
fwrite($handle, "Line 2\n");
flock($handle, LOCK_UN);
fclose($handle);

// Create only if not exists
file_put_contents('new.txt', 'content', LOCK_EX);
File Info & Directories: File functions: basename(), dirname(), pathinfo(), filesize(), filemtime(), filetype(). Directory functions: mkdir(), rmdir(), scandir(), glob(). Recursive directory iteration with RecursiveDirectoryIterator.

<?php
// File info
$path = '/path/to/file.txt';
echo basename($path);      // file.txt
echo dirname($path);       // /path/to
echo filesize('file.txt');
echo filemtime('file.txt');

// Directory operations
mkdir('newdir', 0755, true);  // recursive
$files = scandir('.');
$txtFiles = glob('*.txt');

// Recursive directory iterator
$it = new RecursiveIteratorIterator(
    new RecursiveDirectoryIterator('.')
);
foreach ($it as $file) {
    if ($file->isFile()) {
        echo $file->getPathname() . "\n";
    }
}
File Uploads: Files are uploaded via POST forms with enctype="multipart/form-data". Access via $_FILES superglobal. Use move_uploaded_file() to store. Validate file type, size, and errors. Beware of security: validate extensions, limit size, scan for malware.

<?php
// HTML form: <form method="POST" enctype="multipart/form-data">
// <input type="file" name="document">

if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'POST') {
    $file = $_FILES['document'];
    
    if ($file['error'] === UPLOAD_ERR_OK) {
        $ext = pathinfo($file['name'], PATHINFO_EXTENSION);
        $allowed = ['pdf', 'doc', 'txt'];
        
        if (in_array($ext, $allowed)) {
            $dest = 'uploads/' . uniqid() . '.' . $ext;
            move_uploaded_file($file['tmp_name'], $dest);
            echo "Uploaded to $dest";
        }
    }
}

GET & POST: $_GET contains URL query parameters. $_POST contains POST body. $_REQUEST combines both (avoid for security). $_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] tells the HTTP method. Use htmlspecialchars() or htmlentities() to prevent XSS when outputting user data.

<?php
// URL: /page.php?name=Alice&age=30
$name = $_GET['name'] ?? 'Guest';
$age = $_GET['age'] ?? 'unknown';

// POST form handling
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'POST') {
    $email = $_POST['email'] ?? '';
    // Always escape output!
    echo htmlspecialchars($email, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');
}
?>
<form method="POST">
    <input type="email" name="email">
    <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
Input Validation: Validate input: filter_var() with FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL, FILTER_VALIDATE_URL, etc. Check string length with strlen(), patterns with preg_match(). Use filter_input() to access and filter in one step. Sanitize with FILTER_SANITIZE_*.

<?php
$email = $_POST['email'] ?? '';

if (!filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) {
    echo "Invalid email";
}

$url = 'https://example.com';
if (filter_var($url, FILTER_VALIDATE_URL)) {
    echo "Valid URL";
}

// Combined access and filter
$name = filter_input(INPUT_POST, 'name', FILTER_SANITIZE_STRING);

// Custom validation
if (preg_match('/^[a-zA-Z ]+$/', $name)) {
    echo "Valid name";
}
Sessions: Sessions store user data across requests. session_start() begins or resumes a session. Store in $_SESSION array. Cookie with session ID is sent to client. Regenerate session ID after login with session_regenerate_id() to prevent fixation.

<?php
session_start();

// Store
$_SESSION['user_id'] = 42;
$_SESSION['role'] = 'admin';

// Retrieve
if (isset($_SESSION['user_id'])) {
    echo "User {$_SESSION['user_id']} logged in";
}

// Regenerate after login
session_regenerate_id(true);

// Destroy on logout
session_destroy();
Cookies: setcookie() sends a cookie to the browser. $_COOKIE reads incoming cookies. Set path, domain, secure, httponly, and samesite for security. Cookies are stored client-side and sent with every request to the domain.

<?php
// Set cookie (expires in 1 hour)
setcookie('theme', 'dark', time() + 3600, '/', '', true, true);

// Cookie with SameSite
setcookie('prefs', json_encode(['lang' => 'en']), [
    'expires' => time() + 86400,
    'path' => '/',
    'secure' => true,
    'httponly' => true,
    'samesite' => 'Lax'
]);

// Read cookie
$theme = $_COOKIE['theme'] ?? 'light';

PDO Connection: PDO (PHP Data Objects) provides a consistent interface for multiple database types. Connect with DSN string. PDO supports prepared statements, transactions, and error handling. Use try/catch for connection errors.

<?php
$dsn = 'mysql:host=localhost;dbname=test;charset=utf8mb4';
$user = 'root';
$pass = '';

$options = [
    PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
    PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => PDO::FETCH_ASSOC,
    PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false,
];

try {
    $pdo = new PDO($dsn, $user, $pass, $options);
    echo "Connected";
} catch (PDOException $e) {
    echo "Connection failed: " . $e->getMessage();
}
Prepared Statements: Prepared statements prevent SQL injection by separating SQL from data. Use named (:name) or positional (?) placeholders. prepare() returns a PDOStatement. execute() binds and runs. Fetch results with fetch(), fetchAll(), or fetchColumn().

<?php
$pdo = new PDO('mysql:host=localhost;dbname=test', 'root', '');

// Named placeholders
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = :email AND active = :active');
$stmt->execute(['email' => 'alice@example.com', 'active' => true]);
$user = $stmt->fetch();

// Positional placeholders
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)');
$stmt->execute(['Bob', 'bob@example.com']);
$id = $pdo->lastInsertId();

// Fetch all
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE age > ?');
$stmt->execute([18]);
$users = $stmt->fetchAll();
CRUD Operations: Create (INSERT), Read (SELECT), Update (UPDATE), Delete (DELETE). Use transactions for multiple related operations. beginTransaction(), commit(), rollback(). Always use prepared statements for any user-influenced data.

<?php
$pdo = new PDO('mysql:host=localhost;dbname=test', 'root', '');

// Create
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)');
$stmt->execute(['Alice', 'alice@example.com']);

// Read
$stmt = $pdo->query('SELECT * FROM users');
$users = $stmt->fetchAll();

// Update
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ?');
$stmt->execute(['Alicia', 1]);

// Delete
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?');
$stmt->execute([1]);

// Transaction
try {
    $pdo->beginTransaction();
    $pdo->exec('UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1');
    $pdo->exec('UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 2');
    $pdo->commit();
} catch (Exception $e) {
    $pdo->rollBack();
}
MySQLi: MySQLi is a MySQL-only alternative to PDO. Supports both procedural and OOP styles. Use prepared statements with $mysqli->prepare(). Procedural functions (mysqli_connect, mysqli_query) are also available.

<?php
// OOP style
$mysqli = new mysqli('localhost', 'root', '', 'test');

if ($mysqli->connect_error) {
    die("Connection failed: " . $mysqli->connect_error);
}

$stmt = $mysqli->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?');
$stmt->bind_param('i', $id);
$id = 1;
$stmt->execute();
$result = $stmt->get_result();
$user = $result->fetch_assoc();

// Procedural style
$conn = mysqli_connect('localhost', 'root', '', 'test');
$result = mysqli_query($conn, 'SELECT * FROM users');
while ($row = mysqli_fetch_assoc($result)) {
    print_r($row);
}

Exceptions: PHP uses try/catch blocks for exception handling. throw new Exception('message') raises an exception. Multiple catch blocks for different exception types. finally block runs regardless of whether an exception occurred (PHP 5.5+).

<?php
try {
    $file = file_get_contents('nonexistent.txt');
    if ($file === false) {
        throw new Exception('File not found');
    }
} catch (Exception $e) {
    echo 'Caught: ' . $e->getMessage();
    echo 'File: ' . $e->getFile();
    echo 'Line: ' . $e->getLine();
} finally {
    echo "This always runs";
}

// Multiple catch
// } catch (PDOException $e) {
//     echo "Database error";
// } catch (Exception $e) {
//     echo "General error";
// }
Error Reporting: error_reporting() sets which errors are reported. Use E_ALL for development. display_errors controls output. log_errors saves to file. set_error_handler() catches non-exception errors. trigger_error() manually triggers errors.

<?php
// Development settings
error_reporting(E_ALL);
ini_set('display_errors', '1');
ini_set('log_errors', '1');
ini_set('error_log', '/var/log/php_errors.log');

// Custom error handler
set_error_handler(function($severity, $message, $file, $line) {
    throw new ErrorException($message, 0, $severity, $file, $line);
});

// Trigger error
trigger_error('Something happened', E_USER_WARNING);

// Restore
restore_error_handler();
Custom Exception Classes: Create custom exceptions by extending Exception. Use different exception classes for different error types. Catch specific exceptions before general ones. SPL exceptions (InvalidArgumentException, RuntimeException, LogicException) cover common cases.

<?php
class ValidationException extends Exception {}
class DatabaseException extends Exception {}
class NotFoundException extends Exception {}

function validateEmail(string $email): void {
    if (!filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) {
        throw new ValidationException("Invalid email: $email");
    }
}

try {
    validateEmail('not-an-email');
} catch (ValidationException $e) {
    echo "Validation error: " . $e->getMessage();
} catch (Exception $e) {
    echo "Other error: " . $e->getMessage();
}

Composer & Autoloading: Composer is the dependency manager for PHP. composer.json defines dependencies. composer install/downloads packages into vendor/. PSR-4 autoloading maps namespaces to directories. require 'vendor/autoload.php' loads everything.
PSR Standards: PSR (PHP Standards Recommendations) define coding standards: PSR-1 (basic coding), PSR-4 (autoloading), PSR-7 (HTTP messages), PSR-12 (extended coding style). Following PSR standards ensures interoperability between PHP packages.

<?php
// PSR-1: <?php tags, side effects separate
// PSR-4: Namespace matches directory structure
// PSR-12: Braces on new line for classes/methods

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Service;

use Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface;
use Psr\Http\Message\ServerRequestInterface;

class UserService
{
    public function handle(ServerRequestInterface $request): ResponseInterface
    {
        // PSR-7 compatible
    }
}
PHP 8 Features: PHP 8 introduced: named arguments, attributes (annotations), constructor property promotion, union types, match expression, nullsafe operator (?->), str_contains(), str_starts_with(), str_ends_with(), readonly properties (8.1), enums (8.1), fibers (8.1).

<?php
